title: High Court extends Abhishek Banerjee's protection from coercive action in six cases
dek: Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya said investigations were incomplete and nothing had changed to justify withdrawing the relief, over the state's objections.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Calcutta High Court on Monday extended interim protection from coercive action for Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee in six criminal cases registered against him at police stations in West Bengal since May. Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya ordered that the protection would last until 26 February 2027 or until further orders, whichever is earlier, according to reports.

Three of the cases, registered at the Bhowanipore, Bishnupur and Kalitala police stations, were covered by protection first granted on 25 August. Additional Advocate General Billwadal Bhattacharya opposed an extension, telling the court that the state had challenged the 25 August order in the Supreme Court and that the appeal was pending. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, for Mr Banerjee, called it a "defective appeal", reports said.

The other three cases, at the Rabindranagar and Bishnupur police stations in South 24 Parganas, were covered by an order of 7 September. Additional Advocate General Rajdeep Majumdar opposed that plea too, and the state filed progress reports on the investigation in two of the cases.

The judge said the investigations were not complete and found no change in circumstances that would justify withdrawing the protection, according to reports. The reports did not describe the allegations in the cases. Mr Banerjee, the MP for Diamond Harbour, is the Trinamool Congress's national general secretary.
